subject: High Detection Probabilities in Sites with No Detections

messages.author: 67eefb0e32c64fae
messages.subject: High Detection Probabilities in Sites with No Detections
parts:
Hello,

Could anyone enlighten me as to why Unmarked is telling me that a site with no detections has a detection probability of 50%? I understand that some sites with no detections may be occupied, and thus have a positive detection, but 50% for a site with no detections seems unreasonably high. I have run into several issues when estimating site-specific detection probabilities using a model with 'site' as the only predictor. Estimates for some sites have huge standard errors, and unusually high detection estimates based on the data. For example, site 30. I believe this to be the fault of a small dataset and overfitting of the model. 

My primary questions are:

1) Should I ignore these results and assume that the errors are caused by small sample size/overfitting?
2) Am I correct in saying that the biases in these estimates will not impact a region-level model, which aggregates count data from several sites?

messages.author: 247b990d236a7af6
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] High Detection Probabilities in Sites with No Detections
parts:
It's not an issue of the printed estimate being too high but rather than you have no information to estimate a detection probability for such sites with no detections (unless you go Bayesian).  The 0.5 is almost certainly the starting value in the iterative fitting procedure.

The other pieces of information are that the estimated confidence intervals go from 0 to 1 and the standard error is way bigger than 1.  (38.63887883 is way to large for a random variable taking on values only between 0 and 1.)

Probably placing a NA for the estimate would be the most appropriate thing to do.

I have to ask:  Why do you need separate estimates of detection probability for each site?  Might there not be available covariates that might explain any differences in detection probabilities among sites?

Jim

Jim,

Thank you for the explanation - that makes sense - I will do as you suggest! To answer your question, this was more of a way to see whether detection probabilities differed among sites. When I put this model into an AICc it performs extraordinarily well, but only because it is over-fit. Fortunately I do have a few site-level covariates to test, including variables describing the structural complexity of a site, and its vegetative cover.

Thank you, Sean
